# Convert a bank or card statement PDF to CSV, and see whether it adds up

> Free bank and credit card statement PDF to CSV converter that proves the result: opening balance plus the transactions must equal the closing balance. CSV for Xero or QuickBooks Online, an Excel workbook (.xlsx) whose running-balance and Check formulas re-prove the rows on every edit, or a bank download file (QBO for QuickBooks, QFX for Quicken, OFX, QIF). Choose a year of monthly statements at once: they are joined in date order and each month's opening balance is checked against the previous month's closing, so a missing month shows as a gap of exactly its amount. Scanned statements and photos are read by OCR in the browser too, with misread figures corrected only where the running balance proves them. Runs in your browser; the PDF is never uploaded.

Reads statements in English, French, Dutch, German, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese, several accounts in one PDF (each proved by its own running balance and totals), and detects card versus bank statements. Measured on an independent public benchmark of statement PDFs: 5 of 5 read to the right row count and proved; on two fixtures from another open-source parser, 62 of 62 rows right and proved, including a statement whose own printed balance is misprinted, which the tool names as a misprint rather than a missing row (method and numbers: eval/README.md in the source). Scans: on 36 degraded synthetic scanned statements, 98.6% of rows read right, 19 of 25 intact statements perfect and none wrong without a warning; all 11 with a row lost from the picture were flagged, not balanced over (eval/scans-2026-11-17.txt). Bank files: twelve files written from made-up statements read the same (rows, net amount, unique transaction ids, ledger balance) by three OFX readers the tool did not write (ofx-file-check, ofxtools, ofxparse; eval/bank-files-2026-11-18.txt); a year of 12 statements with June left out is flagged with a gap equal to June's net movement. Excel: on 11 workbooks LibreOffice recalculated all 830 formulas to the tool's own values, 0 of 3,280 cells different (eval/xlsx-check-2026-11-22.txt). Not yet tested on a real customer's statement or a real scan, or by importing into QuickBooks or Quicken themselves.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.
